title: Training Diffusion Language Models for Black-Box Optimization
claim: A unified text corpus of heterogeneous signals feeds a staged adaptation and post-training procedure that aligns a model with high-scoring outputs.
layout: 3 panels: top corpus construction, bottom-left adaptation, bottom-right SFT+RL; color-coded token grids
description: The figure has three dashed-border panels. Panel (a), at top, shows a color-coded prompt: orange boxes hold natural-language instructions, green boxes hold offline DNA designs with labels wrapped in delimiter tokens, and a blue box holds the response design. Brackets mark q (the prompt) and o (the response). A large teal arrow leads to a database icon labeled Unified Prompt–Response Corpus, D_text = {(q,o)}. Panel (b), bottom-left, covers Domain Adaptation. It shows grids of colored tokens, with gray noisy masked tokens, being denoised into complete grids. Panel (c), bottom-right, covers Post-Training. caption: Overview of the DiBO framework. (a) Unified Prompt–Response Corpus: Heterogeneous BBO signals (natural-language prompts, offline designs and their associated labels) are unified using explicit delimiter tokens. (b) Domain Adaptation (DA): The diffusion LLM is domain-adapted via joint masked-token prediction over prompts and responses. (c) Post-Training: The model is further aligned with high-label designs via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) based on label improvements.
abstract: We study offline black-box optimization (BBO), aiming to discover improved designs from an offline dataset of designs and labels, a problem common in robotics and DNA with limited labeled samples. While recent work applies autoregressive LLMs to BBO by formatting tasks as natural-language prompts, their left-to-right design generation struggles to capture the strong bidirectional dependencies inherent in design problems. To address this, we propose adapting diffusion LLMs to offline BBO to leverage their bidirectional modeling capabilities. However, a domain gap exists between the natural text pre-training of diffusion LLMs and the heterogeneous signals in BBO (prompts, designs, and labels). To bridge this gap, we construct a unified prompt--response corpus and introduce delimiter tokens to explicitly mark field boundaries for domain adaptation. We further propose a two-stage post-training framework to align the diffusion LLM generation with high-label designs. The first stage performs supervised fine-tuning on the unified dataset via masked-response prediction, and the second stage adopts reinforcement learning with rewards defined by label improvements. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on Design-Bench under small-data settings with highly efficient training, requiring only $1.5$ H100 GPU hours for discrete tasks. Code for our work is available here: https://github.com/zpointS/DiBO.
